items.title: Ward 5 Councillor Pushes Council to Study Mississauga's Illegal Dumping Hot Spots
items.summary: According to mississauga.com, Ward 5 Councillor Natalie Hart is bringing a motion to city council on Sept. 29 aimed at tackling illegal dumping and littering across Mississauga. The motion asks staff to study how the city can keep public spaces cleaner, covering parks, neighbourhoods and commercial areas alike. If council approves it, staff would identify locations where dumping keeps recurring and evaluate ways to address them, from changes in operational practices to site design and where waste bins are placed. The motion also directs staff to look at public education efforts, including multilingual communications, to help reach the city's diverse communities with information on proper waste disposal and reporting tools. Staff would additionally consider expanding the city's Be a Good Neighbour and neighbourhood standards pilot program, which has been running in Ward 5 since August 2025, to other parts of the city. The pilot's record so far could help shape how far the broader anti-dumping push extends.

items.title: Malton Station Loses VIA Rail Service Starting Late October
items.summary: According to Insauga, VIA Rail is ending train service at its Malton station on Derry Road East in north Mississauga, effective Oct. 25. The Crown corporation says the move is meant to improve overall travel times as part of a schedule review it announced in mid-September. That same review initially proposed permanently cutting all service to Guildwood station in Scarborough, but VIA Rail reversed course last Friday after backlash from commuters, meaning trains will keep serving that Toronto depot beyond Oct. 25. VIA Rail is also adjusting other stops along its Quebec City to Windsor corridor as part of the twice yearly review. Saturday service on trains 68 and 69 will be replaced by new departures on trains 668 and 669. VIA Rail says the revised schedule is meant to better match service with passenger demand and make the network more reliable and predictable.

items.title: Mississauga Joins National Push to Mark Truth and Reconciliation Day on Sept. 30
items.summary: According to Modern Mississauga, Canadians are marking the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation on Sept. 30, a day that coincides with Orange Shirt Day and its Every Child Matters message. Established in 2021, the day recognizes residential school Survivors, their families and their communities, while working to keep the history of residential schools from being forgotten. Canadians are encouraged to wear orange in honour of Survivors and in memory of the children who never returned home. In Ottawa, the Peace Tower and the Senate Building will be illuminated in orange throughout the evening to mark the occasion. APTN and the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation are also hosting a National Commemorative Gathering called Remembering the Children, open to Canadians who want to take part. The observance has grown from a grassroots initiative into a nationally recognized day of remembrance, education and reflection observed by individuals, organizations and communities across the country, including in Mississauga.

items.title: High-Risk Ontarians Can Get Free Flu and COVID Shots Starting Today, With Wider Rollout Next Month
items.summary: According to mississauga.com, Ontario has begun rolling out free flu and COVID-19 vaccines this week, starting with high-risk groups before opening to the general public next month. Hospital staff and patients, residents and staff at long-term care and retirement homes, and people in other congregate living settings can get the shots immediately, along with anyone 65 and older. The province says most other residents will have to wait until Oct. 26 for their turn, while infant RSV immunization is set to begin Oct. 1. Availability may vary between individual pharmacies and health care providers even within the eligible groups. The vaccines are meant to reduce the spread of serious flu and COVID-19 symptoms heading into the colder months. The Government of Canada notes that flu symptoms typically appear one to four days after exposure, and can include fever, cough, muscle aches, chills, fatigue, sore throat and a stuffy nose. Left untreated, the flu can worsen existing chronic conditions and lead to pneumonia, heart complications or respiratory failure requiring hospitalization. Federal data cited in the report puts the flu among the top ten causes of death in Canada, linked to roughly 3,500 deaths a year.

items.title: Credit River Salmon Begin Their Annual Push Upstream From Lake Ontario
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, the annual salmon run is underway along the Credit River as thousands of fish leave Lake Ontario each fall to swim upstream and spawn. The migration typically begins in September, peaks in early October and continues through the fall depending on weather and water conditions. Guided by instinct, the salmon return to the same waters where they hatched, battling strong currents along the way. Once they reach calmer water, they dig a gravel nest called a redd, where they lay their eggs before their life cycle ends. The city calls it one of Mississauga's most remarkable wildlife events, drawing residents to local parks and trails each year to watch the fish fight their way home. Officials are asking anyone heading out to observe the run to do so respectfully and let the salmon complete a journey they have spent years preparing for.

items.title: Lithium-Ion Battery Fires Take Center Stage as Mississauga Marks Fire Prevention Week
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, Mississauga Fire and Emergency Services is using this year's Fire Prevention Week, running Oct. 4 to 10, to focus on the risks of charging lithium-ion batteries. The week's theme, Charge Into Fire Safety: Safe Charging Is a Superpower, targets the everyday habits people use when charging phones, laptops, tablets, e-bikes, e-scooters and power tools. MFES says lithium-ion batteries have become the city's fastest-growing ignition source, with battery-related fires up 122 percent in 2025 compared with the year before. Officials warn that these fires can start suddenly, spread quickly and are often difficult to put out once they begin. Residents can meet MFES members at locations around the city throughout the week to learn more about safe charging and other fire safety topics. Fire Prevention Week is observed across North America each year as a chance for residents to review emergency plans and refresh their knowledge of fire risks facing homes and communities.

items.title: Provincial Funding Boost for Peel Police Follows Steep Drop in Local Auto Thefts
items.summary: According to Insauga and CBC Toronto, Peel Regional Police auto theft numbers have kept falling, dropping from 3,089 vehicles stolen between January and June of 2025 to 2,790 over the same six months this year. Peel police Chief Nishan Duraiappah said the force has made real progress but wants to keep the pressure on organized crime groups behind the thefts. The comments came as Ontario Solicitor General Michael Kerzner visited Peel police headquarters in Mississauga on Monday to announce part of a new $6 million provincial commitment to fighting auto theft, with $300,000 of that earmarked for Peel police specifically. Kerzner credited the funding and added police resources for the province wide decline, while cautioning that the fight is not over. Data from Equite Association's 2025 auto theft trend report shows vehicle thefts across Ontario fell to 19,319 last year, down 36 percent from a peak of 30,134 in 2023.

items.title: Mississauga Partners With Vox Pop Labs to Launch Vote Compass Ahead of Oct. 26 Election
items.summary: According to mississauga.com, the city has partnered with Vox Pop Labs to launch Vote Compass, a free tool meant to help residents see how their views on local issues line up with those of candidates running in the Oct. 26 municipal election. With the election approaching, candidates are canvassing neighbourhoods, sharing their platforms at community events and posting their priorities on social media, while lawn signs around the city serve as a reminder of the choices on the ballot. City officials say making an informed choice is not always easy, and that many residents who skip voting point to not feeling informed enough as a reason. Vote Compass is designed to give voters a clearer sense of where candidates stand before they head to the polls. The tool is being made available to residents in roughly 50 Ontario municipalities holding elections this year, not just Mississauga.

items.title: Mississauga Library Pitches Its Free Card as One of the City's Best Money-Saving Tools
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, a free library card is being promoted as one of the most valuable items residents can carry in their wallet as living costs continue to climb. Mississauga Library says the card unlocks far more than book borrowing, including movies, video games, online learning courses, career resources and family programming that would otherwise require paid subscriptions. Thousands of digital titles are available to borrow anytime through the library's online collection, alongside access to magazines, newspapers and other trusted news sources from around the world. The library frames itself as more than a lending service, describing its branches as community spaces where people can learn new skills, attend events and build connections regardless of age, income or background. Officials are encouraging residents who have not signed up to get a card and explore what the system offers, from career support to language learning resources.
